desc: The UAP Task Force was approved by Deputy Secretary of Defense David L. Norquist on 4 August 2020 and announced by the Navy on 14 August 2020, sited in the Department of the Navy with Office of Naval Intelligence involvement and cognizance by the Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence and Security. Its stated mission was to detect, analyse and catalog UAP that could potentially pose a threat to US national security. It is the most consequential body in this domain because it did two things no successor has done: it produced the classified substrate of the ODNI Preliminary Assessment delivered to Congress on 25 June 2021, and - per David Grusch's sworn testimony - its director tasked a cleared intelligence officer to identify every special access programme relevant to the Task Force's congressionally mandated mission, a tasking that ran directly into refused read-ons. Jay Stratton is publicly identified as its director in the operative 2020-2021 period. The Task Force was disestablished by direction of the 15 July 2022 AARO establishment memorandum, which ordered the Secretary of the Navy to shut it down and transfer its data and materials to AARO. That transfer is a custody event: everything the UAPTF held about crash retrieval allegations, if it held anything, passed into an office reporting to the Deputy Secretary of Defense.

claims.text: Deputy Secretary of Defense David L. Norquist approved establishment of the UAP Task Force on 4 August 2020; the Department of the Navy, under the cognizance of the Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence and Security, was designated to lead it.
The establishment was announced publicly on 14 August 2020.
The UAPTF mission of record is 'to detect, analyze and catalog UAPs that could potentially pose a threat to U.S. national security.'
The Office of the Director of National Intelligence published 'Preliminary Assessment: Unidentified Aerial Phenomena' on 25 June 2021, drawing on UAPTF work.
The 25 June 2021 ODNI assessment covers 144 reports originating from U.S. government sources, primarily U.S. military aviators, for incidents occurring between November 2004 and March 2021.
The 25 June 2021 ODNI assessment was accompanied by a classified annex; the unclassified body attributes only one of the 144 reports with high confidence.

claims.text: On 23 November 2021 Deputy Secretary of Defense Kathleen Hicks directed the Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence and Security to establish the Airborne Object Identification and Management Synchronization Group (AOIMSG) as successor to the Navy's UAP Task Force, with an Airborne Object Identification and Management Executive Council (AOIMEXEC) providing oversight.
AOIMSG was placed under the Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence and Security, then held by Ronald Moultrie.
AOIMSG was superseded in July 2022 by the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO), producing three differently named organizations covering the same subject matter within a 24-month period.

David Grusch served as the National Reconnaissance Office representative to the UAP Task Force from 2019 to 2021, and from 2021 to 2023 as his agency's co-lead for UAP and trans-medium object analysis at the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency.
In 2022 Grusch filed a whistleblower complaint with the Intelligence Community Inspector General that was found credible and urgent for transmission to the congressional intelligence committees.

claims.text: On 26 July 2023 Grusch testified under oath before the House Oversight Subcommittee on National Security, the Border, and Foreign Affairs, describing himself as a former NRO representative to the UAP Task Force and stating he had been informed of a multi-decade crash retrieval and reverse-engineering program to which he was denied access.

AARO's 2024 Historical Record Report Volume 1 states that AARO 'has no evidence for the USG reverse-engineering narrative provided by interviewees' and assesses that named alleged reverse-engineering programs either do not exist, are misidentified authentic sensitive programs, or resolve to 'an unwarranted and disestablished program.'
The UAPTF's public charter as published contains no reference to materials custody, acquisition authority, or reverse engineering; its stated functions are detection, analysis and cataloguing.

connections: David Norquist and Kathleen Hicks: consecutive Deputy Secretaries who created and dissolved the same body. The Hicks name also appears on the DoD side of the 2023-2024 KONA BLUE declassification correspondence with DHS.
David Grusch's UAPTF billet is the documented conduit between the compartmented world and the House Oversight Committee. He is the single node linking NRO, NGA, UAPTF, the ICIG, and the 2023 hearing.
Ronald Moultrie (USD(I&S)) supervised both the UAPTF's parent office and AOIMSG, and testified before Congress on UAP in 2022.
Luis Elizondo's claimed OUSD(I) AATIP activity and the UAPTF share the same OUSD(I&S) reporting chain a decade apart.

The ODNI preliminary assessment's classified annex is the unreleased counterpart to a public document that Congress has repeatedly cited; it is the most concretely identified withheld UAP record in the modern era.

AARO, the third-generation successor, is the entity that later issued the KONA BLUE narrative and the Historical Record Report, meaning the successor to the task force is also the author of the government's denial.
The FY2024 NDAA UAP Records Collection at NARA is the statutory downstream of records the UAPTF generated.
dossier.denialPosture: DoD has never denied the UAPTF existed; it published its own establishment. The denial operates one level down, at AARO, which states in its 2024 Historical Record Report Volume 1 that it has found no evidence of any U.S. reverse-engineering program and that interviewees, including those with UAPTF-adjacent access, 'likely' misinterpreted sensitive but conventional programs because 'none of the interviewees had firsthand knowledge.' The denial is an assertion about the mental states of named witnesses rather than a document production.
dossier.narrative:
The establishment is on the record and unambiguous. The Navy's own press release of 14 August 2020 states: "On Aug. 4, 2020, Deputy Secretary of Defense David L. Norquist approved the establishment of an Unidentified Aerial Phenomena (UAP) Task Force (UAPTF). The Department of the Navy, under the cognizance of the Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence and Security, will lead the UAPTF." The mission statement is "to detect, analyze and catalog UAPs that could potentially pose a threat to U.S. national security." Note what is absent: any reference to materials, recoveries, or prior programs. The public charter is a sensor-and-safety charter.

What the UAPTF actually produced was the dataset in the ODNI preliminary assessment delivered 25 June 2021, prepared in response to a reporting provision attached to the Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021. That nine-page unclassified assessment, with a classified annex, covers 144 reports from U.S. government sources between November 2004 and March 2021, states that most reports came from Navy and other military aviators, and identifies a small number of cases where UAP "appeared to remain stationary in winds aloft, move against the wind, maneuver abruptly, or move at considerable speed, without discernable means of propulsion." The assessment explicitly declines to attribute the phenomena and cites limited, inconsistent reporting as the principal analytic constraint. It is the government's own written acknowledgment that a body of unexplained aerospace observations exists inside its own sensor record.

The personnel question is where the task force becomes load-bearing for the program argument. David Grusch, an Air Force veteran and intelligence officer, served as the NRO representative to the UAPTF from 2019 to 2021 and then as his agency's co-lead for UAP and trans-medium object analysis at the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency from 2021 to 2023. In 2022 he filed a complaint with the Intelligence Community Inspector General that was found credible and urgent for reporting to the congressional intelligence committees. On 26 July 2023, under oath before the House Oversight Subcommittee on National Security, the Border, and Foreign Affairs, Grusch testified that in the course of his official duties he was informed of a multi-decade crash retrieval and reverse-engineering program to which he was denied access, and that recoveries included non-human biologics. Whatever one concludes about the substance, the provenance is institutional: the claim entered the public record through a person whose job was to represent a national intelligence agency to a DoD task force.

The dissolution is as instructive as the founding. On 23 November 2021 Deputy Secretary of Defense Kathleen Hicks, in coordination with the Director of National Intelligence, directed the Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence and Security to establish the Airborne Object Identification and Management Synchronization Group as the successor to the Navy's UAPTF, with oversight from an Airborne Object Identification and Management Executive Council drawn from DoD and the intelligence community. Ronald Moultrie was the USD(I&S) of record. AOIMSG itself lasted months before being reconstituted in July 2022 as the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office. Three names, three charters, three sets of reporting relationships, in under two years, for the same subject matter. Each transition reset what Congress had been briefed on and who owed the briefing.

The naming precision matters here in the same way it matters for AATIP. The UAPTF was a Navy-led DoD task force with an OUSD(I&S) reporting chain. It was not a special access program, it did not have acquisition authority, and nothing in its public charter gives it custody of anything. That is precisely Grusch's point: he says the compartmented activity he learned about was adjacent to, and walled off from, the body Congress had been told was handling the subject. The UAPTF is therefore best read on this board not as the program but as the sensor that detected the program from inside the building.

Who matters by name: Norquist (approving authority), Hicks (dissolving authority), Moultrie (USD(I&S)), Grusch (NRO representative), and the ODNI and Navy officials who signed out the June 2021 assessment. What the record shows is a legitimate, publicly chartered analytic body producing a public product that concedes unexplained observations. What the record does not show is any UAPTF authority over, or access to, materials — and the absence of that authority in a body specifically created to be the government's answer on UAP is the anomaly worth pulling on.
openQuestions: The 4 August 2020 Norquist approval memorandum itself has not been released in full. What does the charter say beyond the press release summary?
Who led the UAPTF day to day, and what was the size and composition of its staff? DoD has never published a roster.
What is in the classified annex to the 25 June 2021 ODNI assessment, and has it been provided to the House Oversight Committee?
Was there an ONI-run UAP task force predating the 4 August 2020 formalization, and if so under what authority did it operate?
Grusch says he was briefed on a program while serving as NRO representative to the UAPTF. Who briefed him, and does the UAPTF hold a record of that briefing?
What happened to UAPTF holdings during the two reorganizations, and were any records destroyed or reclassified in transit?
dossier.whatItIs: The Unidentified Aerial Phenomena Task Force (UAPTF) was a Department of Defense body approved by Deputy Secretary of Defense David L. Norquist on 4 August 2020 and announced publicly on 14 August 2020, led by the Department of the Navy under the cognizance of the Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence and Security. Its stated mission was to detect, analyze and catalog UAP that could potentially pose a threat to U.S. national security. It produced the dataset behind the June 2021 ODNI preliminary assessment and was superseded in November 2021 by AOIMSG and in 2022 by AARO.
dossier.whyImplicated: The UAPTF is where the modern disclosure fight acquired its documents and its witnesses. David Grusch served as the National Reconnaissance Office representative to the UAPTF, and it was from inside that role that he says he was briefed on, and then denied access to, a multi-decade crash retrieval and reverse-engineering program. That is the specific institutional pathway by which a legacy program's existence leaked into a body that Congress could subpoena. The task force also demonstrates the concealment mechanism in miniature: a Navy-led, OUSD(I&S)-supervised body with an unclassified public face and a classified annex, stood up only after decades of the same phenomena being handled through channels Congress was not shown. Within fifteen months of its public announcement it was dissolved and its functions moved twice, each time into a differently named organization with different reporting lines. Reorganization is a documented concealment technique on this board, and the UAPTF-to-AOIMSG-to-AARO chain is the cleanest recent example of it.
